title: openai-chat-completions-parity-params-roles-stop-logprobs-formatting-streaming
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Bring /v1/chat.completions parity (params, roles, stop, logprobs, formatting) into Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer and stabilize streaming + structured output formatting. This PR maps OpenAI-style request params to Redwood internal API, fixes role handling edge-cases, preserves stop token semantics across multi-part streaming, and surfaces logprobs when requested. It also includes a number of streaming stability fixes to reduce partial-message duplicates and ensure function/tool call boundaries are emitted correctly.

Summary of changes: - API: add openai_compat layer to translate params (temperature, top_p, n, max_tokens, stop, logprobs, presence_penalty) to Redwood runtime call options. - Roles: normalize system/user/assistant role handling to match OpenAI precedence and message trimming rules. - Stop/logprobs: implement multi-stop token handling in the streamer and wire up logprobs generation path for compatibility mode. - Streaming: fix race between chunking and KV cache eviction that produced duplicate tokens for long-running streams; add unit/integration tests covering streaming resume and stop token enforcement. - Structured output/formatting: ensure content-format fields (e.g., delta vs final, function call metadata) follow OpenAI-compatible shapes for SDK consumers. - SDKs/docs: update Python/TS SDK OpenAI-compat wrappers and add examples + migration notes.

Testing: Extensive unit tests added for param mapping, role precedence, stop enforcement, and logprobs serialization. Integration tests exercise streaming over 30s sessions with randomized chunk boundaries to validate stability. CI matrix ran against internal runtime stable and beta kernels. Local load tests show negligible latency regression (<1%) and a 3-7% improvement in streaming tail behavior due to batching adjustments.

Rollout: Feature gated under runtime feature-flag `openai_compat_v2`. Default for hosted API remains current behavior until a staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) after additional canary in prod. Backwards compatibility: existing Redwood API consumers unaffected unless opt-in.

Checklist:
- [x] Param mapping and validation
- [x] Role normalization and trimming
- [x] Stop token enforcement in streaming and non-streaming paths
- [x] Logprobs serialization under compatibility mode
- [x] Streaming stability unit/integration tests
- [x] SDK wrappers and docs update
- [x] Performance regression testing

Related: Linear ENG-1428 (Chat parity spec), ENG-1435 (streaming stability), related PRs for structured output formatting.
